{"candidate_rtl":"module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire reverse_sub = ~Oper[2] & Oper[1] & ~Oper[0];
    wire subtract = Oper[0];
    wire arithmetic_enable = ~Oper[2] & (~Oper[1] | ~Oper[0]);
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_a = reverse_sub ? b : a;
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_b = reverse_sub ? a : b;
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_result = arithmetic_a + (arithmetic_b ^ {64{subtract}}) + subtract;

    always @(*) begin
        if (arithmetic_enable) begin
            sum = arithmetic_result;
        end else begin
            case (Oper)
                3'b011: sum = a | b;
                3'b100: sum = a & b;
                3'b101: sum = a ^ b;
                3'b110: sum = a ~^ b;
                default: sum = 64'b0;
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule","bottleneck":"The dominant path is the 64-bit carry-propagate add/subtract datapath followed by operation selection into sum.","rewrite":"Factor the three arithmetic operations into one shared conditional two's-complement adder, use a compact arithmetic-enable decode for opcodes 000 through 010, and retain an explicit logic-operation case for exact opcode behavior and the zero default.","expected_timing_gain":"Expected modest improvement from sharing the adder and reducing arithmetic-result selection depth; estimated maximum data arrival around 2.7-2.9 ns, subject to synthesis mapping.","area_or_other_cost":"Likely lower or comparable mapped area because the three arithmetic cases share one adder and subtraction inversion network. No additional state, storage, or interface logic is introduced.","functional_boundaries":"Exact for all 64-bit a and b values and all 3-bit Oper values. Arithmetic results are modulo 2^64, matching the original sum truncation; opcodes 011, 100, 101, and 110 produce OR, AND, XOR, and XNOR respectively, while opcode 111 produces all zeros."}
